newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher after retail price hike.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher after retail price hike.

text.p: CSCE nearby coffee futures shot up Tuesday as speculators went on a buying spree after a major U.S. roaster announced its plans to pass on higher world green coffee futures prices to consumers, traders said.

"When roasters raise their retail prices, they are probably foreseeing it's going to be awhile before they can buy cheap coffee," one trader said. "Their stockpiles are almost non-existent and the tightness might continue for at least a few more months."

The spot May contract surged 6.25 cents on the day to 226.50 cents a lb, ending just shy of a new life-of-contract high of 227.00 cents set earlier in the session. On the continuous weekly chart, May's finish was the highest since September 1994.
Benchmark July arabicas ended up 2.55 cents at 198.95 cents after ranging between 201.50 and 196.00 cents, while the back months closed 2.00 higher to 3.00 lower.

Coffee prices defied pre-opening expectations and headed higher at the outset. Traders said upward momentum accelerated after the July contract breached 200.00 cents resistance and word spread around the floor that Procter & Gamble's Folgers Coffee Co raised its 13-ounce cans of ground coffees by 20 cents.
The increase, which was to take effect immediately, brought the new price for Folgers' standard can of regular coffee to $3.06, and decaffeinated ground Folgers up to $3.76, the company said.

"The list price of Folgers coffee generally reflects the price of green coffee sold on the commodity market," Folgers said in a statement. "Green coffee prices have been rising since January, and have continued due to a number of factors including reduced crop estimates for the upcoming harvest in Brazil, reduced availability of coffee from Central America and Colombia, and the generally tight supply of arabica beans on the worldwide coffee market."
Traders and analysts said they expect supply concerns to continue to bolster the market.

"With the overall fundamentals, nobody's going to bet on this market going lower," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "The combination of tight stocks and indictations of a smaller Colombian crop all point to this market going higher"
Reflecting tight nearby availability, the May/July switch ballooned to 27.45 today from 23.85 at the close on Monday.

The exchange reported after Monday's close that certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 48,603 60-kg bags -- or about 195 lots -- as of April 25. Open interest on the May contract, which expires in three weeks, stood at 2,486 lots.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 1,500 bags, to 47,103 bags as of April 28. There were 3,000 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,932 lots.
